hypothesis: Appending one bounded shell-to-total-mass fraction will reduce fixed-HGB holdout MAE by at least 0.05 rings because it exposes a biologically motivated allocation interaction as one axis-splittable feature.
mechanism: The feature represents shell mass relative to the larger magnitude of shell or whole mass. My inference is that this may summarize cumulative allocation to calcified shell versus total body mass and let histogram trees threshold that relationship directly. The cited biology paper supports coupled shell deposition, calcification, and organismal growth, but does not establish that this weight ratio predicts rings. OpenFE supports division-based binary feature construction, while the tree paper shows that boosted trees split individual feature axes; neither demonstrates improvement for this task.
why_new: This is distinct from the rejected constant median-residual calibration: it changes the input representation using two measured columns and performs no prediction postprocessing. It is a single, first-order arithmetic interaction—the smallest mechanism proposed here—not a claim of methodological novelty.
feature_rationale: abs(row[9]) is shell-weight magnitude. The denominator max(max(abs(row[6]), abs(row[9])), 0.000001) uses whole-weight and shell-weight magnitudes, bounds the result to [0,1], and remains defined when either or both inputs are zero. The sole constant, 0.000001, is frozen as a numerical zero guard; it is not fitted, scaled, or selected from data. No other constants or candidate variants are proposed.

evidence.claim: Rudraraju et al. model molluskan development as coupled mantle volume growth, shell secretion, surface accretion, and calcification. This supports treating shell and whole-organism measurements jointly, but not the proposed formula or an association with ring count.

OpenFE's methods enumerate first-order binary transformations including division, then evaluate whether generated features add predictive value. This supports a prespecified ratio as a legitimate feature-construction mechanism, not its effectiveness here.

Chen and Guestrin describe boosted-tree split finding as thresholding individual feature columns. I infer that explicitly supplying a ratio can expose a compact threshold coordinate that otherwise requires multiple axis-aligned splits; the paper does not test this feature, fixed HGB, or Abalone.

limitations: This is only a proposal for human review; it is not registered, approved, executed, or validated.
No data, labels, predictions, or benchmark outcomes were accessed or reconstructed, and no model was trained. Consequently, the direction and magnitude of any gain are unknown.

The only task-specific comparisons are historical aggregate MAEs: HGB 1.4852994049871073, ridge 1.5698357707260964, and median 2.3538283062645013. These weak aggregate baselines provide no uncertainty, split sensitivity, subgroup behavior, or evidence for this feature.
The biological source concerns general molluskan morphogenesis rather than Abalone ring prediction or measured mass fractions; applying it here is explicitly an inference.
The tree-method source concerns XGBoost rather than the frozen histogram gradient boosting implementation, so the axis-split argument is structural rather than implementation-specific evidence.

If reviewed and authorized, the frozen protocol must use the stated six fits, unchanged rows, original columns, HGB parameters, and controls. GO requires every seed and the mean to gain at least 0.05 ring MAE, a positive paired-row bootstrap lower bound, and latency ratio at most 1.1.
The three seeds are repeatability checks, not independent training evidence. Bootstrap interpretation remains conditional on the fixed training set because row independence is unverified.

Any valid below-threshold result is STOP for this mechanism, with no constant adjustment, parameter rescue, added feature, retry, or post-rejection revision. Invalid measurement closes the attempt without a scientific conclusion or automatic retry.
Compute, transformation, timing, wall-time, RSS, byte, and actual monetary costs remain unknown until an authorized run and must not be treated as zero.
